26476e6e3fea3e1b2ffe.text: Let us understand the different rules in formulating an information question or the wh-question.

ebdfc61394232859e2f4.text: Wh-Questions Wh-questions begin with what, when, where, who, whom, which, whose, why, and how. We use them to ask for information. The answer cannot be yes or no.

334f26ace23ab9f88965.text: A: When do you finish high school? B: Next year. A: Who is your favorite actor? B: Lee Min Ho for sure!

c514196bbec942a08cc3.text: We usually form wh-questions with wh- + an auxiliary verb (be, do or have) + subject + main verb or with wh- + a modal verb + subject + main verb:

rows: Have: What has she done now?
Modal: Who would she stay with?
49d2756db428d1e59cdd.text: Be: When are you leaving? Who’s been paying the bills? Do: Where do they live? Why didn’t you call me? Have: What has she done now? What have they decided? Modal: Who would she stay with? Where should I park?

c6ddb03598efe73e6c20.text: When we ask negative wh-questions, we use the auxiliary verb do when there is no other auxiliary or modal verb, even when the wh-word is the subject of the clause:

rows: Who doesn’t want an ice cream?

b026d53a70faef8915da.text: For better understanding, here are some examples of simple and thought-provoking questions. Study the examples carefully and see how they differ from each other.

rows: 1. How does the pandemic impact the global economy?
2. What are ways to prevent COVID- 19?
2. What are some ways by which people from your community can make a difference during the pandemic?
3. How should you wash your hands?
3. How can we combat people’s misconceptions about COVID-19?

07e30635e155b1dc8eb4.text: questions. To recap, what are the

0a8b0f24a77753d01c82.text: things you should consider in asking

c010275f8fff76e68a4a.text: Yes, raising sensible, challenging thought-provoking questions can

c65dabb86706aa972c2d.text: stimulate, draw out, and guide a discussion.

394a1d52a780060f9f0c.text: We don’t always hear everything we want to hear in the exact order, depth,

68b406b6ac3dc3b58717.text: and detail; thus, it is important to know how to formulate and raise questions that are sensible, challenging, and thought-provoking.

981f1dfb3cf1088e6e15.text: Here are tips on how to perfect your questions:

3a47f7330043347acbbd.text:  Research first. If you still have questions and the opportunity is available, you should do your own research before asking the question. Knowing as much as you can about the subject before asking the question is the most important part about asking a question intelligently. That you are acquainted with the subject will show when you talk about it.  Compare what you know and what you don’t. Before you ask, think about what you do know about the topic and what you don’t know. Do you have a lot of information and only need small details? Do you know almost nothing? The more information you know about a topic, the more intelligent your questions can be.  Consider your goal. You need to decide what the intended goal of your question is. What will the answer help you accomplish, really? This will be helpful in deciding what information you require from the person you’re asking. The more specifics you know about what you need, the more intelligent your questions will be and the smarter you will appear.

d65b1a02d443b081957b.text:  Look for points of misunderstanding. Examine what you know about the topic and what you’re confused about. Are you sure about the things that you do know? Oftentimes what we think we know creates questions that don’t really have answers because our initial information was wrong. It may be a good idea to do some basic fact checking, if you can.  Try looking at the issue from all sides. It may be possible to answer your own questions, by looking at the problem from all sides. A new approach may help you see something you couldn’t see before, resolving any problems you had on the issue.
